_publicationNotice: Sanitized historical record, not a new test or operational approval. Identifiers are placeholders; original private evidence is retained separately. Recorded statuses/times/results are historical, not current state. Sanitized bytes cannot verify original hashes.
scope: Local PowerShell AST-extracted functions with mocked Graph/authentication/sleep, in-memory cleanup ledgers, and a real Save/deserialization round trip using a removed session-only synthetic ledger; no live Apply/Restore entrypoint executed.
concurrencyLimit: Mocked fresh reads and optional ETag forwarding are tested. No claim of Graph atomic compare-and-swap when no ETag is supplied; serialize external consent writers.

assertions.assertion: The helper parses without executing its top-level entrypoint.
Consent watchdog uses only its unique approved event name.
Consent mutation mutex is independent of the MFA watchdog.
The helper never references the existing MFA ledger, event, or policy mutation endpoints.
Absent grants have empty baseline arrays, not null-element arrays.
Each exact target receives one POST with verified composite identity.
Initial private intent ledger precedes all mutations; per-target saved intent is checked by each mock POST.
Owned empty grants are deleted and verified absent.
AllPrincipals and admin Principal grants remain canonically unchanged.
No unrelated grant is ever mutated.
Ledger deserialization preserves approval precision and timezone as a string.
Deserialized ledger validates and restores both mocked grants.
Both live-ledger read sites explicitly preserve JSON date strings.
Real Save-InstallConsentRecord writes its atomic ledger to a session-only test file.
Actual restore-read pipeline retains exact approval/deadline strings and passes strict record validation after real Save.
Actual restore-read pipeline retains exact approval/deadline strings and passes strict record validation after real Save.
First-principal failure does not postpone the second cleanup until retry.
Only the failed principal is retried.
Successful restoration retains the transient error in the persisted ledger.
Permanent cleanup failure is explicit and cannot claim success.
Six bounded attempts for the failed principal do not abort the other cleanup.
Bounded retry backoff is 5, 15, 30, 60, and 120 seconds.
Final ledger records the outstanding target and every failed attempt.
A lost POST response is reconciled by exact composite identity without a second POST.
Uncertain response is persisted even after successful reconciliation.
Reconciled introduced grant is safely removed.
Durable mutation intent survives losing both POST response and immediate reconciliation.
Restore locates the target by composite identity without a captured grant ID or POST replay.
Preexisting approved scope is not recorded as introduced.
Cleanup retains preexisting approved and unrelated concurrent scopes.
A preexisting grant is never deleted.
New grant with an unrelated concurrent scope is patched, not deleted.
Entire grant deletion is avoided when unrelated scope is present.
Fresh pre-delete read catches a newly added unrelated scope and switches to PATCH.
No stale empty-scope observation causes DELETE.
Service-provided ETag is forwarded on the mutation.
Already absent grants and repeated restoration require readback only, never new mutations.
Ambiguous duplicate composite targets are not modified.
First-target duplicates do not block independent second-target cleanup.
